newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher but still rangebound.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher but still rangebound.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended Thursday higher in a late, albeit small, pickup in buying interest, but the entire complex was still confined in its recent price range.
"We're just bouncing up and down the range," said an East Coast paper broker.

The market was wakened briefly from its current lull by early reports that restart of the 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit would be postponed until early March. But most players shrugged off the news by late morning.

Southern California Edison said it would likely extend the outage of San Onofre 2 nuclear power plant in San Clemente, Calif., into early March. SoCal Edison discovered Wednesday a tube leak in a main generator at the unit.

San Onofre 2 was shut Nov 30 for refueling and was set to resume power production between February 22 and 28. Its return to service was already delayed once earlier this month for repairs needed on the steam generators.
March California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up 15 cents at $10.45 a megawatt hour (MWh) after trading between $10.25 and $10.50.
April COB finished up 10 cents at $9.95. Active deferred COB contracts ended flat to 15 cents higher.
March Palo Verde (PV) settled up 24 cents at $13.54, near its session high of $13.55.
April PV finished up 15 cents at $12.55. Active back-month PV contracts ended mixed.
Firm, peak day-ahead power slipped 50 cents at COB to $9.50-10.50 and rose about 75 cents at PV to $12.25-13.00.

The Northwest River Forecast Center today trimmed its outlook of spring runoffs for hydroelectric projects in the Pacific Northwest. Its latest update showed January to July runoff on the Columbia River at The Dalles dam in Oregon would hit 132 percent of average, compared with an estimate in early February of 137 percent.
In the Pacific Northwest, forecasts called for lingering showers Thursday, then mild air this weekend with temperatures climbing through the weekend.
Northwest temperatures were expected to be near normal Thursday but were called to climb to five to 10 degrees above normal Friday through Tuesday.
Longer-term forecasts called for above and much-above normal temperatures through the western half of the U.S. from Feb 25 to March 1.

In the Southwest, forcasts called for some showers and mountain snow Thursday and Friday, then dry weather Sunday through Tuesday. In general, temperatures there were expected to be six to 12 degrees above normal by early next week.
NYMEX estimated 115 COB and 96 PV contracts were sold, compared with Wednesday's sales of 117 COB and 66 PV lots.
